name: Future Forms
description: Will, be going to, present forms with future meaning, Future Continuous and Future Perfect, and future time clauses.

questions.title: Look at those clouds. It ___ any minute now.
The phone is ringing. Don't get up, I ___ it.
We ___ dinner with the Petrenkos on Saturday. The table is already booked.
The museum ___ at nine o'clock every day, including Sunday.
Which form expresses a decision made at the moment of speaking?
I have already decided. I ___ apply to a technical university.
Which sentence about future time is correct?
options: I will call you when I arrive.
I will call you when I will arrive.
I call you when I will arrive.
I am calling you when I will arrive.

questions.title: Do you think prices ___ next year?
Our flight ___ at 6.40 tomorrow morning.
Which sentence offers help?
options: Shall I carry that bag for you?
Do I carry that bag for you?
Am I carrying that bag for you?
Will I carrying that bag for you?

questions.title: She ___ twenty next month.
Which word signals a future time clause where 'will' is not used?
There is no bread left. I ___ some on my way home.
What does 'be about to' express?
options: something that will happen in the very near future

questions.title: Match each future form with the sentence that illustrates it.
pairs: That looks heavy. I will help you.
be going to for an intention
I am going to study medicine.
I am meeting the dentist at four.

questions.title: Match each situation with the most natural future form.
pairs: making a prediction based on evidence

questions.title: Match each sentence beginning with the ending that completes it.
pairs: I will text you as soon as
We are going to move house

questions.title: Match each future expression with its meaning.
This time next week I ___ on a beach in Odesa.
By the end of the course you ___ over two hundred new words.
Which sentence describes an action that will be in progress at a future moment?
options: At eight tomorrow we will be driving to Kyiv.
At eight tomorrow we will drive to Kyiv.
At eight tomorrow we will have driven to Kyiv.
At eight tomorrow we drive to Kyiv.

questions.title: Don't call me at seven. I ___ my exam then.
By 2030 the company ___ in business for half a century.
Which sentence is the most polite way of asking about somebody's plans?
options: Will you be using the printer this afternoon?
Are you going to use the printer this afternoon?
Do you use the printer this afternoon?
Will you use the printer this afternoon?

questions.title: He ___ the report by Friday, so we can discuss it at the weekend.
Which future time clause contains a mistake?
options: I will tell her when I will see her.
I will tell her when I see her.
I will tell her after I have seen her.
I will tell her the moment I see her.

questions.title: The negotiations ___ to continue until late in the evening.
What is the difference between 'I will see him' and 'I will be seeing him'?
options: The second suggests a meeting that will happen in the normal course of events.
The second is more urgent than the first.
The second refers to a shorter action.
There is no difference in meaning.

questions.title: We had better hurry, or we ___ the last bus.
By the time you read this letter, I ___ the country.
I doubt whether the parcel ___ before the weekend.
Match each future form with the exact meaning it carries.
pairs: I will be working at nine.
I will have worked eight hours by then.
I will have been working since dawn.

questions.title: Match each sentence with the speaker's intention.
pairs: I promise I will pay you back.
I am going to complain to the manager.
Will you close the window, please?

questions.title: Match each time linker with the tense that follows it in a future sentence.
pairs: present simple with a precautionary meaning

questions.title: Match each prediction with the evidence type behind it.
pairs: She will probably enjoy the film.
The forecast says it will freeze.
Interest rates are set to rise.

questions.title: Match each faulty future sentence with the reason it is wrong.
pairs: I will go shopping when I will finish work.
will is not used in a time clause
evidence calls for be going to
The train will leave at 9.05 every day.
a timetable needs the present simple
I am going to help you with that suitcase.
a spontaneous offer calls for will

questions.title: Should the funding be approved, construction ___ next autumn.
Which sentence is the most formal way of announcing a scheduled event?
options: The ceremony is to take place on 12 May.
The ceremony is taking place maybe on 12 May.
The ceremony will be taken place on 12 May.
The ceremony is going to happen on 12 May.

questions.title: Delegates ___ to register before the opening session.
Which sentence expresses an unavoidable future consequence?
options: Such a policy is bound to provoke criticism.
Such a policy is likely provoking criticism.
Such a policy will be provoked criticism.
Such a policy provokes criticism tomorrow.

questions.title: On no account ___ the building before the alarm is switched off.
Which sentence correctly uses the future perfect continuous?
options: By June she will have been teaching here for thirty years.
By June she will have taught here since thirty years.
By June she will be teaching here for thirty years already.
By June she is teaching here for thirty years.

questions.title: Match each formal future structure with its meaning.
pairs: The minister is to visit the region.
The train is due to arrive at noon.
The reform is set to take effect in July.

questions.title: Match each sentence with the degree of certainty it expresses.
Match each future structure with the register in which it is typical.
pairs: We are to convene at ten.
We will be convening at ten.
